name: Adjektiv
subtitle: Adjectives: agreement, definite form and comparison

ruleCards.title: Three forms: rolig, roligt, roliga
ruleCards.rule: An adjective agrees with its noun. En-words take the base form, ett-words add -t, and plurals add -a. This works both before the noun and after är.
ruleCards.watch: Look at the noun, not the adjective: filmen är rolig (en-word), huset är stort (ett-word).

ruleCards.title: The definite form: -a
ruleCards.rule: After den här, det här, de här (and den, det, de + adjective) the adjective always ends in -a, and the noun takes its definite ending too.
ruleCards.watch: Double definite: den stora bilen has both den and -en.

ruleCards.title: After my, your, his: -a
ruleCards.rule: After possessives (min, din, hans, hennes, vår, deras …) and after a name with -s, the adjective also ends in -a. The noun stays in its basic form.
ruleCards.watch: No definite ending on the noun here: min stora bil, not min stora bilen.

ruleCards.title: Liten: four forms
ruleCards.rule: Liten is irregular. En-words: liten. Ett-words: litet. Plural: små. Definite and after possessives: lilla.
ruleCards.watch: Plural is always små, also in the definite: de små barnen.

ruleCards.title: Ny → nytt, god → gott, röd → rött
ruleCards.rule: Adjectives that end in a stressed vowel add -tt for ett-words. Adjectives that end in vowel + d drop the d and add -tt.
ruleCards.watch: Bra never changes: en bra bok, ett bra jobb, bra böcker.

ruleCards.title: Comparison: -are and -ast
ruleCards.rule: Most adjectives add -are for “more” and -ast for “most”. Use än for “than”.
examples: The bus is cheaper than the taxi.
ruleCards.watch: Never add mer to a short adjective: billigare, not mer billig.

ruleCards.title: Irregular comparison
ruleCards.rule: A few common adjectives change their vowel or the whole word. Learn them as sets of three.
ruleCards.watch: Never gammalare or storare: äldre, större.

ruleCards.title: Mycket, mer, mest vs många, fler, flest
ruleCards.rule: Things you can’t count (kaffe, tid, vatten, pengar) take mycket – mer – mest. Things you can count (bilar, vänner, böcker) take många – fler – flest.
ruleCards.watch: Pengar looks plural but you can’t count it: mycket pengar, mer pengar.
